newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM SEES COPPER LEVELS AT LOWEST IN APRIL.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM SEES COPPER LEVELS AT LOWEST IN APRIL.

text.p: Poor fuel supplies to Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines could push copper production down by 9,457 tonnes in April, a ZCCM official said on Wednesday.
The official told Reuters ZCCM had forecast that production at month end was likely to reach 17,600 tonnes compared to 32,050 in March -- one of the lowest levels in ZCCM's history.
Production in April was expected to be 9,457 tonnes below the estimated output of 27,057 tonnes, he said.

"The shortfall is largely on account of the shortage of heavy fuel oil due to low supplies from Indeni (the local petroleum refining company) which hampered production, particularly from Nkana and Mufulira smelters during March and April 1997," the official said.
He said poor fuel supplies from Indeni forced the closure of the Mufulira smelter from March 28 to April 12, and some operations at the Nkana smelter had been closed between March 28 and April 16.
"The shutdown of the Nkana smelter furnance resulted in the cessation of acid production from Nkana with consequent losses of production for the Nchanga tailings leach plant," the spokesman said.

"Further production losses were incurred at Nchanga Division following the shutdown of the Nchanga Open Pit which resulted in the suspension of overburden removal activities from March 28 to April 11.
"This was due to the critical diesel shortage, as all the available diesel was sent to Ndola Lime Company for lime production...to keep the cobalt plant in operation", the official said.
ZCCM was expected to meet its 25,442 tonnes production target for May if fuel supplies improved, he said.
